source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν τοὺς τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἀδιαφόρως πρὸς γάμου κοινωνίαν συνάπτειν τὰ ἑαυτῶν παιδὶα αἱρετικοῖς. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Δέν πρέπει οἱ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας (1) ἤτοι τόσον Κληρικοί, ὅσον καὶ οἱ λαϊκοὶ ὀρθόδοξοι να ὑπανδρεύουσι τὰ τέκνα τῶν μὲ αἱρετικούς, χωρὶς να κάμνουσι καμμίαν διαφορὰν ὀρθοδόξου ἀπὸ αἱρετικοῦ. Ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τὸν ιδ΄. τῆς δ΄.
thought_title: No indiscriminate marriage of church children to heretics
orientation: The council is issuing its tenth canon, now forbidding members of the church from marrying their children to heretics without distinction.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning that it is not necessary for those of the church to join their own children to heretics indiscriminately for the communion of marriage. Interpretation. Those of the Church, that is, both clergy and orthodox laity, must not marry their children to heretics, without making any distinction of orthodox from heretic. Read also the fourteenth of the fourth.

lemmas.gloss: to marry off, give in marriage

choices.why: The adverb modifies the joining in marriage, meaning without making a distinction between orthodox and heretic; 'indiscriminately' captures the lack of discrimination.
The phrase denotes the shared bond or fellowship constituted by marriage; 'communion of marriage' preserves the noun κοινωνία as 'communion' per the glossary.
The verb means to bind or unite together; 'join' is literal and fits the context of marriage alliance.
The verb is causative, meaning to give in marriage; 'marry off' conveys the parents' action of arranging marriage for their children.
The phrase explicitly negates any differentiation between orthodox and heretic; 'without making any distinction' is literal and clear.

pass_b_english: Concerning the rule that members of the church must not join their children in the communion of marriage with heretics indiscriminately. Interpretation: Those of the church—that is, clergy as well as orthodox laity—must not marry off their children to heretics without making any distinction between orthodox and heretic. Read also canon 14 of the Fourth.

problems.quote: See also Canon 14 of the Fourth Council.
problems.source_quote: Ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τὸν ιδ΄. τῆς δ΄.
problems.why: τῆς δ΄ means the 4th canon, not the Fourth Council. This is Canon 4 of this same council.
problems.ruling: τῆς δ΄ abbreviates τῆς δ΄ συνόδου (Fourth Council), but context shows this IS Canon 4 itself, not referencing Canon 14 of Fourth Council; 'τῆς δ΄' alone is ambiguous but standard abbreviation for council, yet claim is right that it means '4th' canon of this council, not 'Fourth Council'

edits.old: See also Canon 14 of the Fourth Council.

fixed: Corrected 'See also Canon 14 of the Fourth Council' to 'See also Canon 4': source 'τῆς δ΄' refers to the fourth canon of this council, not the Fourth Council.

problems.source_quote: Ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τὸν ιδ΄. τῆς δ΄.
problems.why: The source cites canon 14 (ιδ΄) of the 4th (δ΄), a council or synod. The English reduces this to 'Canon 4', which names a different canon and drops the number 14.
problems.fix: Read also canon 14 of the Fourth.

edits.new: Read also canon 14 of the Fourth.

fixed: See also Canon 4. -> Read also canon 14 of the Fourth (source: Ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τὸν ιδ΄. τῆς δ΄.)

last_rejected.quote: join their children in the communion of marriage with heretics indiscriminately
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'join their children to heretics', not 'heretics to marriage'; 'communion of marriage' overtranslates κοινωνίαν γάμου as a technical phrase rather than 'marriage alliance/partnership'.
last_rejected.fix: must not give their children in marriage to heretics without discrimination
last_rejected.ruling: ἀδιαφόρως renders 'indiscriminately'; κοινωνίαν γάμου = 'communion/partnership of marriage' is standard, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: marry off their children to heretics
last_rejected.why: Greek ὑπανδρεύω means 'give in marriage' (of giving daughters to husbands), not 'marry off' which implies active arranging; more critically, the Greek specifies 'their children' (τὰ τέκνα) but the context and Canon 14 show this means 'give daughters to heretic men'.
last_rejected.fix: give their children in marriage to heretics
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπανδρεύουσι τὰ τέκνα = 'marry off their children'; 'marry off' is normal range; restricting to daughters is interpretation, not translation error.
